findings.note: addForced (plan.mjs:140-153) maps a mutant's start/end through d.oldToNew[start]/[end] without the containing()-based fallback used elsewhere (plan.mjs:262-263) for lines inside a hunk. It is only reached after hunkIntersects has already returned false for every hunk, so in every path exercised by plan.test.mjs the endpoints are outside changed hunks and the mapping is always defined; not a credible normal-usage failure given the residual/hunk edge cases (block open/close, insertion, deletion, capped diff) are all covered by tests. Flagging as hardening only in case a future hunk-adjacency change lets addForced see an endpoint that touches a deletion.

resolveViews's failure message at views.mjs:453 appends r.error.message when present, but spawnSync's own timeout kill (VIEWS_TIMEOUT_MS at views.mjs:440) does not reliably populate r.error with an ETIMEDOUT-style message on all platforms -- the unit test at views.test.mjs simulates {status:null, error: new Error('ETIMEDOUT')} directly rather than exercising a real timeout, so a genuine hang would likely surface only 'failed (exit null)' without naming the cause. This is a diagnostics/UX gap, not a functional failure: the command still fails safely as a UsageError (exit 2) either way.
